data.source_title: Improving daily patient room cleaning: an observational study using a human factors and systems engineering approach
data.locator: Methods: unit of observation and observation period; Results, Table 6
data.source_setting: Eight adult medicine inpatient units at a 1,059-bed urban academic medical center in Baltimore, Maryland; daily room cleaning by day-shift environmental care associates
data.source_n: 89 observed room-cleaning episodes; 10 day-shift environmental care associates
data.quantity: Observed room cleans with at least one interruption
data.source_evidence_basis: At least one interruption occurred in 50 of 89 observed cleans; the paper reports 56% (50/89; calculated 56.2%). Interruptions included patients/families, EVS colleagues, other healthcare workers, missing supplies and environmental events. The paper does not quantify extra elapsed time caused by each interruption.
data.limitations: Single academic center, convenience sample, adult medicine units and daytime observations; isolation status, patient presence, interruptions and unit type varied. This entry-to-exit elapsed time can include interruptions and is not a pure hands-on labor measure or microbial efficacy measure. Do not treat it as total post-discharge unavailability.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use only as an external sensitivity anchor for an occupied-room cleaning task. Model post-discharge notification, EVS response/wait, cleaning, inspection and bed-ready signal as separate events requiring local calibration.

data.source_title: Improving daily patient room cleaning: an observational study using a human factors and systems engineering approach
data.source_setting: Eight adult medicine inpatient units at one urban academic medical center, Baltimore, Maryland
data.source_n: 89 observed daily room-cleaning episodes; 10 day-shift environmental care associates
data.quantity: Room cleans with at least one interruption
data.source_evidence_basis: At least one interruption occurred in 50 of 89 observed cleans (reported as 56%). Interruptions included patients/families, EVS colleagues, other healthcare workers, missing supplies and environmental events. The paper separately reports median active cleaning time; it does not quantify extra elapsed time caused by each interruption.
data.limitations: Single-site convenience sample and direct observation; categories can co-occur. This is a daily occupied-room cohort, not a discharge-clean or turnover distribution, and the percentage is not a target-site probability.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Represent interruption as an optional pause or task switch in an external EVS workflow sensitivity scenario; do not add a duration or transfer the cohort probability without local timestamp data.
